- APM breakdown (pi-ext/core/prompts/apm-breakdown.md line 75) deliberately substitutes priority tiers for DC's user-story tags: DC desglosar format is [TID] [P?] [Historia] Descripción with mandatory [US#] tags and Phase 3 grouped per story with cross-story parallelism, while APM uses [TID] [P?] [Priority] Description because APM has no user-stories artifact (only .feature Gherkin scenarios tagged @P1/@P2/@P3, per apm-breakdown.ts header comment). Cost of dropping [US#]: no scenario-level traceability, no cross-story parallelism (P2 waits for all P1 even when disjoint), no story-level completion accounting. Proposed fix: extend format to [TID] [P?] [Priority] [Scenario] Description with scenario slug from .feature so an importer gets requirement_keys free. *(2d ago)*
- completed: GAP-055 canonical cutover is green across the Go cmd/pic suite (144/144); fresh databases no longer create or probe legacy epics/tasks workflow tables, while workflow_schema.go retains only one-way import support and main.go retains a legacy-only invalidation trigger guarded from fresh databases. *(10d ago)*
- Lean claim invariant: the activePacks COUNT query must be re-run after prepareInstructionPackForFirstClaim on worker stage claims — hoisting the count before prepare caused the exactly-one-active-pack check to see a stale count of 0 and broke TestProfileLifecycleIntegration; caught and fixed in the lean routing restructure. *(1d ago)*
- Lean claim path design for imported/lean tasks: claim = status flip to in_progress plus claimed_at/claimed_by plus one work_item_events row; worker input is the stored description verbatim; completion = status done plus event (no completion-report row since its pack columns are NOT NULL); review/verification reference task+run without pack columns; the single non-negotiable retained invariant is single-writer exclusion. *(1d ago)*
- User decided on the hybrid option: disable task-system's local /agents command and use pi-subagents-lite's /agents instead; the local /agents registration in pi-ext/subagent/ui.ts was commented out and AgentRunsOverlay deleted while keeping the footer tracker. *(1d ago)*
- Terminal-signal failure mechanism: the 'agent process exited without a terminal result' string comes only from tracker.sync() salvage (invoked from ui.ts updateFooter on every panel refresh), which fires only for runs still marked running whose pid is dead or process-identity-mismatched — so the five completed wi-9ed6a1e6 scouts were marked failed because the spawning extension host was gone/reloaded before their exit events could finalize them; the runner finish path defaults stopReason to end/error on exit but salvage trusts only <completion_report status="done"> or <review_report> verdicts in the last message (event summaries capped at 4000 chars, so any fix must match an opening <scout_evidence tag with section attribute). *(6d ago)*
- authorize_work_item_implementation binds the currently checked-out branch: the Pi tool wrapper (tool.ts:446) auto-derives branch-name from git branch --show-current and hardcodes base-branch develop (base-commit from refs/remotes/origin/develop with local fallback), so authorizing from develop fails; the Go side also requires the authorizing aggregate's OWN approved task_graph checkpoint, so the coordinating Epic wi-42d42701 cannot be branch owner without running its own vision/blueprint/contracts/task_graph ceremony (precedent epic wi-36f86b96 had its own task_graph); per docs/aggregate-delivery-workflow-spec.md features are branch owners by default, epics coordinators by default, integration:branch/integration:coordination labels override, exactly one aggregate per containment path may own the branch, and automatic branch naming/creation/checkout is an explicit non-goal left to the owner. *(6d ago)*

- Root cause of the 'agent process exited without a terminal result' bug is a three-defect chain, filed as bug wi-33853584: runner.ts (~line 350) spawns detached:true with piped stdio and finalizes only on child.on("close"), so bash grandchildren holding pipe write-ends defer close and finish() never runs; tracker.ts:176 sync() (1s, driven by ui.ts updateFooter) marks dead-pid running runs failed 226ms after the done completion report; scheduler persists pipeline_runs status=completed with no work_item_completion_reports row, no patch, no review. Proposed fix: finalize on child.on("exit") with close as idempotent guard, salvage runs whose final message contains a done completion report, and never mark completed without a durably persisted completion report row; regression tests required for exit-before-close and no-completed-without-report. *(11d ago)*
- Terminal-signal design rationale from nicobailon/pi-subagents (reference cloned to /tmp/pi-subagents-ref; context7 must use libraryId /nicobailon/pi-subagents, not libraryName): pi-subagents makes success a contract via schema-validated structured_output tool plus durable process-terminal proof files (process-terminal-candidate.json with exit code/signal/process-group verification) and layered failure classification, while the task-system runner keys success on exitCode 0 plus tracker.finish with only regex salvage fallback — the minimum viable adoption is reading a host-side completion artifact first rather than importing the full machinery. *(6d ago)*
- wi-9ed6a1e6 resume plumbing: the scheduler sets spec.resumeFailureMode from the last failed worker pipeline run for the pack (PipelineRunRecord carries result_json, error, instruction_pack_id), conditioning on a prior failed run rather than session resumability, and the runner builds the resume preamble (failure mode, git status --short sample, retained-or-fresh note, fresh-deadline notice, no-stash WORKTREE DISCIPLINE rule) inside startSubagent with no task-worker.md change; the no-stash line applies to every worktree-isolated mutation stage run because git refs/stash is shared across linked worktrees, the worker deadline stays 30 minutes since each resume spawns a new process timer, and GAP-140 and SQ-1 need no code changes (fresh-deadline-per-resume supersedes the deferred SQ-1 owner decision). *(4d ago)*

- Parallel-review base-change serialization is a designed guard, not a defect: when sibling reviews share a base commit and one integrates first, the others fail assertReviewBaseCurrent (pi-ext/pipeline/integration.ts:74, 'review base changed before integration; a fresh review is required') with empty result_json and no integration, requiring fresh reviews against the moved HEAD; a second related guard, finalizeReviewedIntegration's staged-diff byte-equality check, refuses integration with 'staged integration differs from reviewed candidate patch' when the candidate patch's pre-image no longer matches (e.g. a later commit touched the same files), leaving staged files in the main repo index that must be reset, and recovery requires regenerating/rebasing the candidate patch against the moved base. *(6d ago)*

- The 'agent process exited without a terminal result' failure in the task-system subagent runner is a deterministic terminal-result transport bug, not a provider crash: tracker.sync() (pi-ext/subagent/tracker.ts:176) marks any still-running run failed when its recorded pid is dead, but tracker.finish() on child close in pi-ext/subagent/runner.ts (with classifyRunnerTransientFault, RUNNER_TRANSIENT_RETRIES=2, resetSubagentWorktreeToCandidate) may not have been called before the child exited, so completed runs are misclassified. It silently loses the worker's done completion_report and persisted patch, while pipeline_runs is marked completed with no work_item_completion_reports row. *(11d ago)*

- The pi-ext pipeline scheduler is event-driven only (queueReconcile via setImmediate, no interval timer); its reconcile sweep includes resumePending (pipeline-scheduler.ts:983) which processes completed non-advanced review runs listed by 'pic workflow pipeline-pending' and calls integrateReviewedCandidate on passed reviews, so triggering a reconcile (e.g. work_on_work_item) integrates an already-passed review with empty integrated_at without a circuit reset. *(6d ago)*

- The runner deliberately keeps spawning workers as isolated pi CLI subprocesses instead of using the @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent SDK, because process isolation survived the fd05ff0 crash class, SIGKILL beats cooperative abort, subprocesses parallelize across cores, and the argv/output contract is stabler than the SDK surface; the assessed migration path when structured per-tool telemetry or live fast-path escalation is needed is pi --mode rpc, which keeps process isolation while adding prompt/steer/abort control and usage-bearing events, but its strict LF-only framing means Node readline must be replaced by vendored pi's reference rpc-client.ts. *(2w ago)*

- Task-system fix-loop mechanics: pipeline-scheduler.ts relaunches failed-review workers as review-fix runs with the rejected patch pre-applied to a fresh worktree plus raw 'REVIEW CORRECTIONS' text (buildReviewCorrections ~line 1063); worker sessions resume via workerSessionPath keyed on instruction-pack ID (.pi/runtime/runs/<packKey>/session.jsonl); runner.ts has GAP-140 guard renaming sessions aside when header cwd no longer exists; review-fix cycles are effectively unbounded until human intervention (only unchanged-TIP autofix has a 3-cycle limit at pipeline-scheduler.ts:1312) and reviewRequiresOwner gates some failed reviews back to owner. *(2w ago)*
- wi-9ed6a1e6 durable worktree design: worker worktrees are keyed by instruction pack at .pi/worktrees/<packId> with a distinct pi-pack-<key> branch prefix (superseding pi-agent-<packId> naming so cleanupOrphanedSubagentWorktrees' pi-agent-/activeRunIds logic stays untouched), pi-pack- branches removed only when older than 24h by mtime, removeSubagentWorktree generalized to accept either prefix with basename(worktree)-equals-key validation, all worker-stage spawns including review-fix relaunches get pack-keyed worktrees while review/scan stages stay run-keyed; an existing owned worktree registered with the expected branch is reused without reset or patch reapplication (initialPatchPath only on fresh creation; review-fix seeds are fresh creations because deterministic terminals clean the worktree; reverse-check fallback covers an already-applied patch), and unregistered or foreign-branch worktree directories fail closed. *(4d ago)*
- Epic wi-42d42701 'Planning artifact upgrades' has reached aggregate verification: verify_work_item on the last descendant returned the full aggregate RRI-T grading prompt with 86 persisted scenarios loaded from artifact wia-6e393d6a rev 1 (sha256:90e38e7a...) covering REQ-1..REQ-9 across QA/Tester, Business Analyst, End User, Developer, and Operator personas, and all 8 descendants are done (wi-c99388e3, wi-155af9fc, wi-e486a1dd, plus verification bugs wi-1424f28e, wi-2df56b25, wi-4ecc16d6, wi-65990a09, wi-b25613fd); aggregate grading must run in the main contractor session and be submitted via verify_aggregate_work_item with rri_t_evidence_json and actor_role=contractor without re-authoring personas, and owner acceptance follows a passed verification. *(3d ago)*
- Go validateRriTVerification (work_items.go ~2982) requires each RRI-T scenario to carry id/persona/dimension D1-D7/stress_axis (TIME|DATA|ERROR|COLLABORATION|EMERGENCY|SCALE|COMPLIANCE|EVOLUTION)/approved requirement_id/procedure/evidence/result PASS|ACCEPTABLE|PAINFUL|FAIL with dedupe on dimension|stress_axis|requirement_id|id, rejects aggregate 'passed' when any scenario is non-PASS, requires concrete reasons on not_applicable rows, and non-passed results create/dedupe a corrective bug; CLI is 'pic work-item aggregate-verify <id> <passed|failed|partial|blocked> <summary> --actor-role contractor [--rri-t-json <json>]'. *(6d ago)*

- In go-pic, next_actions.go nextActionHints maps each stage (scan, rri, vision, blueprint, contracts, task_graph, materialize, authorize, implement, contractor_verification, aggregate_verification, owner_acceptance, merge_pending) to structured NextAction steps with actor roles; task_graph approval carries the five owner granularity questions (too coarse/fine, independently meaningful verification, genuine blockers, horizontal exceptions, merge/split); workItemCheckpointDecide batches owner stage decisions (stage:accepted|approved, scan requires accepted) in one transaction with applyRriGlossaryApproval and CONTEXT.md restore-on-rollback compensation. In profile.go, work_item_profiles rows are version-bound per profile_name plan/implement/qa with planning_depth quick/standard/designed/full; lifecycleForStage maps scan..task_graph to plan, worker to implement, review/autofix to qa; planStagesForProfile gives standalone executables and quick/standard depths scan+rri+task_graph, designed adds blueprint, full adds vision+contracts; ensureWorkItemProfiles resolves profiles exactly once and reuses persisted rows to keep profile lineage immutable. *(2d ago)*

- There is no re-review transition in the scheduler: a failed review verdict is persisted state and the only repair path is review-failed → review-fix worker round (--review-fix 1, capped at REVIEW_FIX_ROUND_LIMIT, then durably blocked for owner approval via 'workflow review-fix-block'); a review-fix worker producing an unchanged patch must report a no_change justification (assertReviewFixChangedPatch) or it is blocked. *(1d ago)*

- completed: the wi-9ed6a1e6 (durable worker worktrees + session resume) Vision was saved as artifact wia-4ddd55d4 rev 1 (stage vision, sha256:7247e160) and owner-approved at 2026-09-03 22:51, advancing the workflow to blueprint; the vision's core shape is one classification branch at persistAgentResult (transient → retain pack-keyed worktree and session with mandatory resume preamble; deterministic → cleanup plus fresh start), SQ-1 fresh deadline per resume, stash forbidden in managed worktrees, GAP-091/096/137/140 supersession rows plus RLB-GAP-001 before code, no new roles/tables/CLI changes, and terminal-signal bug fixes out of scope. *(4d ago)*
- wi-9ed6a1e6 worktree reuse and resume plumbing: an existing owned worktree registered with the expected branch is reused without reset or patch reapplication (initialPatchPath only on fresh creation; review-fix seeds are fresh creations because deterministic terminals clean the worktree; reverse-check fallback covers an already-applied patch) while unregistered or foreign-branch worktree dirs fail closed, and prepareSubagentWorktree already accepts a key parameter so the minimal change is the pack key plus a durable flag; the scheduler sets spec.resumeFailureMode from the last failed worker pipeline run for the pack (conditioned on a prior failed run, not session resumability) and the runner builds the resume preamble (failure mode, git status --short sample, retained-or-fresh note, fresh-deadline notice, no-stash WORKTREE DISCIPLINE rule) inside startSubagent with no task-worker.md change, the no-stash line applying to every worktree-isolated mutation stage run because git refs/stash is shared across linked worktrees (the wi-ed1ce591 attempt-2 stash leak happened on a first attempt). *(4d ago)*
- The wi-9ed6a1e6 resume plumbing: the scheduler sets spec.resumeFailureMode from the last failed worker pipeline run for the pack (PipelineRunRecord carries result_json, error, and instruction_pack_id), conditioning on a prior failed run rather than session resumability, and the runner samples git status --short in the worktree and builds the resume preamble (failure mode, status sample, retained-or-fresh note, fresh-deadline notice, no-stash WORKTREE DISCIPLINE rule) inside startSubagent with no task-worker.md change; the no-stash line applies to every worktree-isolated mutation stage run, not only resumed ones, because git refs/stash is shared across linked worktrees (the wi-ed1ce591 attempt-2 stash leak happened on a first attempt); the worker deadline stays 30 minutes since each resume spawns a new process timer, so GAP-140 and SQ-1 need no code changes and fresh-deadline-per-resume supersedes the deferred SQ-1 owner decision on resumed-session deadline semantics. *(4d ago)*
- apm-spec quality rules: every spec must contain at least one P1 happy-path and one P1 sad-path scenario plus at least 2 measurable success criteria; [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers keep the spec tagged @draft until resolved with the owner (the @ready gate); artifacts are .apm/specs/<domain>/<Name>.feature and .apm/specs/<domain>/requirements.md (empty checklist) always, and .apm/specs/db_schema/<domain>.dbml only if missing; DBML is auto-generated as @provisional and ratified fields are never edited, only extended. *(3d ago)*
- wi-9ed6a1e6 resume plumbing: the scheduler sets spec.resumeFailureMode from the last failed worker pipeline run for the pack (PipelineRunRecord carries result_json, error, instruction_pack_id; conditioned on a prior failed run rather than session resumability) and the runner samples git status --short and builds the resume preamble (failure mode, status sample, retained-or-fresh note, fresh-deadline notice, no-stash WORKTREE DISCIPLINE rule) inside startSubagent with no task-worker.md change; the no-stash line applies to every worktree-isolated mutation stage run, not just resumed ones, because git refs/stash is shared across linked worktrees (the wi-ed1ce591 attempt-2 stash leak happened on a first attempt); the worker deadline stays 30 minutes since each resume spawns a new process timer, so GAP-140 and SQ-1 need no code changes (the existence-based cwd guard keeps pack-keyed sessions resumable and fresh-deadline-per-resume supersedes the deferred SQ-1 owner decision). *(4d ago)*

- pi-ext scheduler tests are source-pattern based: pipeline-scheduler.test.ts tests stagePrompt via regex matching on the stage-prompts.ts source (readFileSync + assert.match), not execution, and there are no real-pic-binary integration tests — only ~140 unit tests, so prompt/prompt-code changes must keep source patterns intact. *(1d ago)*
- RRI-T persona authoring is save-before-execution and all-or-nothing: runRriT fans out all five personas via Promise.all and persists the rri_t_scenarios artifact only if every persona validates in one round, so each retry re-runs the whole fanout (~5 minutes per round, partial success discarded); compileRriTSubmission requires every persisted scenario to carry a result, so trimming the scenario list is impossible without re-authoring — the only lever is a new artifact revision. *(5d ago)*
- go-pic code conventions relevant to the artifact-file work: atomic writes follow the os.Rename precedent (pipeline.go:832/875, work_items.go:2969), events are inserted via addEventWithModel (cmd/pic/workflow.go:164) with id 'wie-'+shortID(), shortID is 8 hex chars from 4 random bytes (main.go:551), and schema migration tests follow the TestDecompositionProjectionMigration precedent (pic_cli_test.go:5123) which builds a pre-v8 baseline DB by hand then runs initDB and asserts version recording plus defaults with once-semantics re-open check. *(2d ago)*
- completed: the LeanTaskClaim bootstrap epic finished all 11 tasks via contractor execution and feature/lean-task-claim was merged to develop as merge commit 0a1809e (11 files, +636/-85); Go suite 226 passed, pi-ext 362 pass/0 fail (known runner flake), and the re-import guard was verified ('already imported: epic wi-0c8b2a01'). *(1d ago)*
- Aggregate RRI-T verification grading rules (from buildAggregateVerifyPrompt in pi-ext/tasking/work-item-prompts.ts): grade in the main contractor session only with no subagents and never grade an unexecuted scenario, exactly one outcome per scenario, ACCEPTABLE requires an owner tradeoff, PAINFUL requires remediation or an explicit owner deferral before acceptance, FAIL blocks aggregate verification, not_applicable needs a concrete reason, and submission is verify_aggregate_work_item with rri_t_evidence_json and actor_role=contractor. *(5d ago)*
- workItemRriFinalize (work_items.go ~1353) validation order: actor-role contractor check, validateRriReport, validateRriReportConsistency, validateRriPublishGate, and validateRriTerminology all run pre-transaction before the approved-scan-checkpoint check in the tx, so publish-gate and terminology-conflict failures occur without needing an approved Scan checkpoint; live-probed error strings include 'RRI publication blocked: open P0/P1 question ... remains unresolved', the resolution-required row-validation error, and the deferred P0/P1 owner-deferral-reason error at work_items.go:1125 (validateRriPublishGate). *(5d ago)*
- wi-9ed6a1e6 resume plumbing: the scheduler sets spec.resumeFailureMode from the last failed worker pipeline run for the pack (PipelineRunRecord carries result_json, error, instruction_pack_id), conditioning on a prior failed run rather than session resumability, and the runner builds the resume preamble (failure mode, git status --short sample, retained-or-fresh note, fresh-deadline notice, no-stash rule) inside startSubagent with no task-worker.md change; a no-stash WORKTREE DISCIPLINE line is appended for every worktree-isolated mutation stage run, not just resumed ones, because git refs/stash is shared across linked worktrees (the wi-ed1ce591 attempt-2 stash leak happened on a first attempt); the worker deadline stays 30 minutes since each resume spawns a new process timer, so GAP-140 and SQ-1 need no code changes (the existence-based cwd guard handles pack-keyed sessions and fresh-deadline-per-resume supersedes the deferred SQ-1 owner decision). *(4d ago)*
- The uncommitted skill-routing evaluation feature in the task-system working tree: pi-ext/pipeline/skill-routing.ts (78 lines) implements observe-mode skill family routing telemetry (evaluateSkillFamilyRouting matching instruction-pack selected families against family.json manifests in packaged task-skills, global ~/.pi/agent/skills, and project .pi/skills via appliesTo tokens), fire-and-forget recording skill_family_routing work_item_events rows at pipeline-scheduler.ts:536; go-pic misc.go skillRoutingForWeb serves GET /api/projects/:id/skill-routing aggregating these events with json_valid-guarded json_extract. *(8d ago)*
- The Work Item model migration is complete: all legacy Task, Epic, and Task Item infrastructure, including backend CRUD, command dispatchers, API routes, and PI extension UI modules, has been systematically removed, making the canonical Work Item model the exclusive state-of-record. *(3w ago)*
- Schema fact for lean verification: work_item_verification_reports.completion_report_id is a nullable FK, so lean verification reports can be inserted without a completion report; the legacy verification-save path (workItemVerificationSave, work_items.go:551) requires the pack-bound integrated completion report, and the legacy completion-save path requires pack-bound pipeline evidence (work_items.go ~518-548). *(1d ago)*
- Aggregate verification mechanics: F2 (wi-155af9fc) re-verification grades all 52 persisted RRI-T scenarios from wia-90842b9c rev 1 verbatim — never re-author or re-run personas, grade in the main contractor session, exactly one outcome per scenario, submit via verify_aggregate_work_item with rri_t_evidence_json {scenarios:[{id,persona,dimension,stress_axis,requirement_id,procedure,evidence,result}]} and actor_role=contractor, and never call owner acceptance in the contractor step; prior aggregate submissions' RRI-T evidence is retrievable from work_item_verification_reports.rri_t_json. *(5d ago)*
- Blueprint tooling payload rules: save_blueprint_draft requires an explicit stage=blueprint argument plus content as one single JSON object (concatenated JSON objects are rejected), and review_blueprint_checkpoint requires actor_role=contractor, artifact_id (the draft id), and content as JSON of the six checkpoint booleans (architecture, design, requirements, verification_seams, task_decomposition, nothing_missing) — a plain 'approve' string or omitted fields are rejected. *(7d ago)*
- Project layout: work_item_artifacts table schema is in go-pic/cmd/pic/workflow_schema.go:53 with UNIQUE(work_item_id,stage,revision) and a 7-stage CHECK constraint; .pi/ is gitignored; APM command implementation lives in pi-ext/core (apm-command.ts, apm-spec.ts, apm-prd.ts, apm-shared.ts, prompts/apm-spec.md, prompts/apm-prd.md). *(3d ago)*
- Task-system escalation and schema facts: resolve_escalation requires id, escalation_id, content (JSON decision/rationale string), and actor_role=contractor because owner answers flow through the contractor rather than actor_role=owner; owner-gated requirement amendments go through amend_work_item_planning with actor_role=owner; SQLite columns are work_item_completion_reports.report_markdown (no content column), work_item_instruction_packs.content_json (task_instruction_packs has no matching rows), and work_item_escalations report_json/resolution_json/resolved_by (no payload_json). *(5d ago)*
- The decomposition-policy-v2 implementation is now present across Go and pi-ext, adding decomposition modes and rationale/pair fields, verification seams, obligation-key checks, edge rationales, and fail-closed v2 validation; review is still in progress, so this is not yet a verified completion. *(9d ago)*
- Large XML evidence bundles are no longer embedded in conversation; instead, they are managed via the EphemeralHandoffStore in pi-ext/core/ephemeral-handoffs.ts, which provides ephemeral IDs for tool-based retrieval with TTL and size-bounded memory storage. *(3w ago)*
- Importer owner decisions (2026-09-06) resolving ApmWorkItemImport.feature NEEDS CLARIFICATION markers: re-import is a hard stop (idempotent update rejected for silent-drift risk); epic/feature naming derives from the .tasks.md Feature field and Phase 3 tier headers with no override flags; the branch is cut at authorization time by the scheduler, never at import; the importer gate verifies a companion .plan.md exists and the .feature is @ready. *(1d ago)*
- The project has initiated GAP-052 to implement a label system for Work Items, following the 'beads' design philosophy (lowercase, unique, create-time assignment, AND/OR filtering); the Go backend and API already fully support label management, while the web frontend and client API layer require updates to expose this functionality. *(3w ago)*
- The current web API implementation in go-pic/cmd/pic/misc.go uses raw SQL for work item updates, which violates the architectural requirement to use the canonical workItemUpdate function in go-pic/cmd/pic/work_items.go for validation and transaction consistency. *(3w ago)*
- pic_cli_test.go test pattern: builds a 'pic' binary in t.TempDir(), uses runPic/runPicError helpers (lines 52/68), dbPath at filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "tasks.db"), and t.TempDir() project roots. *(2d ago)*
- pi -e test runs from /tmp auto-load the global task-system extension via discovery, so use pi -ne to isolate; pi-subagents-lite's Agent tool does not register in headless pi -p print mode, so headless validation of agent types is impossible. *(1d ago)*
- go-pic schema migration architecture (schema_bootstrap.go): ordered one-shot transactional schemaMigrationSteps versions 1-9 (pre_reconcile_schema, artifact_stage_widening, pipeline_columns_reconcile, canonical_baseline, legacy_schema_bootstrap, canonical_backfills, legacy_pack_backfills, decomposition_policy_projection, blueprint_annotation_evidence); legacyOnly steps skip databases without tasks/epics tables; each step runs on one pinned *sql.Conn with foreign_keys=OFF and legacy_alter_table=ON pragmas, recording its version in schema_migrations inside the same transaction. *(2d ago)*
- Owner chose to keep the RRI-T persona agent model cliproxy/ds-4-flash (pi-ext/agents/rri-t-persona.md line 8) and keep retrying rather than switching models, after three consecutive empty_output authoring failures on ~95KB persona prompts; agent definitions are re-read per spawn via discoverAgents so a model-line change would not require a Pi extension reload. *(6d ago)*

- User was confused about when/how skills trigger; assistant explained: commands are explicit (user-typed slash command, deterministic) while skills trigger implicitly — the agent pattern-matches the task against each skill's frontmatter description; don-cheli's HABILIDAD.md has an 'activacion:' field of trigger phrases that is the trigger contract. Failure modes: overlapping trigger vocab, no feedback/log of trigger decisions, near-miss descriptions, phantom triggers from broad descriptions. Practical rules: put concrete phrases in descriptions, keep vocabularies disjoint, promote must-always-run skills to commands, or explicitly name the skill. Rule of thumb given: 'command = you want it, skill = the agent should want it.' *(2d ago)*
